assays: skeletal muscle (vastus lateralis biopsy) and serum EV; long, small and circular RNA-seq (abstract; GEO overall_design)
primary_estimand: within-protocol acute exercise response of the skeletal-muscle long-RNA (protein-coding) transcriptome: h3 and h24 post-exercise vs pre, paired within subject, separately for TRAD (n=21) and HITT (n=19); between-protocol difference in that response as secondary
scope_selected: skeletal muscle long-RNA counts only (GSE209880_muscle_long_counts.txt.gz). Serum EV and small/circular RNA streams are out of scope for 'how exercise affects gene expression' and are not analysed here.

factors.subject: PH id, 40 subjects, each sampled at all three muscle time points

inclusion: 40 young adults randomized to TRAD (12M/9F) or HITT (11M/8F) (abstract)
planned_contrasts: TRAD h3 vs pre (abstract: DE 'within ... exercise protocols' at h3)
TRAD vs HITT response at h3 and h24 (abstract: 'between exercise protocols'; exact model not stated)
repeated_measure_unit: subject (pre/h3/h24 biopsies from the same person)
paper_method: not stated in the abstract or GEO record (full text not available)
paper_results: abstract gives no DEG counts or named genes; only that TRAD generally elicited a stronger transcriptional response than HITT, and more consistent protein-coding gene responses to TRAD
